directions.description: Train on random causal prefix windows to expose older transitions currently omitted by suffix truncation. The [original NextItNet implementation](https://github.com/fajieyuan/WSDM2019-nextitnet) discusses subsequence training and sequence-length sensitivity. Improvement on these four datasets remains a hypothesis.
directions.implementation: Start every experiment from the supplied corrected NextItNet baseline. For this direction, retain its architecture and BPR loss; change only training-window sampling. After selecting a user, use the complete training history with probability 0.5; otherwise choose end = random.randint(2, len(history)) and use history[:end]. Apply the existing reverse-fill sampler to that prefix, preserving left padding and seq[t] -> pos[t] alignment. Exclude the user's complete training interaction set when sampling negatives. Start with maxlen=128; consider 64 only as a subsequent validation-driven trial. Shared requirements for all four directions: retain all four category routes; DATA_DIR = os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR']; training seed 42 and existing preprocessing seed 0; exactly 200 batches per epoch and at most 200 epochs. Keep one independently trained checkpoint per category and write artifacts beneath the trial directory. Expose log2feats(sequence) as encode_sequence(sequence), retain item_emb, and implement predict_score(features, items) using the same scoring head as training. Read out the maximum index where sequence != 0. Preserve the supplied ModelView contract. Update checkpoint metadata and write_predict_script whenever architecture or scoring changes. Select trials using host validation macro HR@10; never combine predictions or checkpoints.

directions.description: Replace single-negative BPR with multiple-negative generalized BCE. The [authors' gSASRec implementation](https://github.com/asash/gsasrec) provides a reusable loss and an [official PyTorch port](https://github.com/asash/gSASRec-pytorch). Transfer only its training objective to NextItNet.
directions.implementation: Keep the supplied causal convolutional encoder, item embeddings, and raw dot-product inference. Start with K=64 negatives per valid target and calibration t=0.75. Sample uniformly from real item IDs, excluding the user's training interactions; do not consult validation labels for training sampling. Flatten only positions with pos != 0 before scoring and chunk negative embedding lookup to limit memory. With positive logits p and negative logits n shaped [N,K], use alpha=K/(itemnum-1), beta=1-t+alpha*t, and loss=(-beta*torch.nn.functional.logsigmoid(p)+torch.nn.functional.softplus(n).sum(-1)).mean()/(K+1). This is the direct gBCE objective, without a transformed-logit approximation. Keep the baseline learning rate initially. Allow patience=40 within the 200-epoch cap because calibrated training can start slowly. K=128 is a subsequent trial if validation and measured GPU cost justify it. Predictor scoring remains unchanged; each category loads its single NextItNet checkpoint.

directions.description: Use BPR-max to focus learning on high-scoring sampled negatives. The [authors' paper](https://hidasi.eu/assets/pdf/gru4rec_v2_cikm18.pdf) and [official PyTorch implementation](https://github.com/hidasib/GRU4Rec_PyTorch_Official) supply the loss. Retain NextItNet throughout.
directions.implementation: Replace the baseline loss independently of the gBCE direction. Start with K=64 uniformly sampled eligible negatives per valid training position. Keep the baseline encoder, optimizer, learning rate, and dot-product scorer. For positive logits p shaped [N] and negative logits n shaped [N,K], compute logw=torch.log_softmax(n, dim=-1); ranking=-torch.logsumexp(logw+torch.nn.functional.logsigmoid(p[:,None]-n), dim=-1); penalty=(logw.exp()*n.square()).sum(-1); loss=(ranking+0.1*penalty).mean(). Use only pos != 0 positions and preserve gradient clipping at 5.0. Evaluate regularization 0.01 or 1.0 only in subsequent trials. Use the identical raw scoring head at inference; the negative weighting belongs solely to training. No separately fitted negative scorer or popularity score is introduced.

directions.description: Add dropout-view contrastive regularization to reduce representation collapse. [DuoRec's paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2110.05730) and [author implementation](https://github.com/RuihongQiu/DuoRec/blob/master/recbole/model/sequential_recommender/duorec.py) motivate stochastic views. Apply the regularizer to the shared NextItNet encoder.
directions.implementation: Keep baseline BPR and add an unsupervised DuoRec-inspired auxiliary loss. Encode each batch twice through the same NextItNet parameters with independent dropout masks. Gather each view at the final nonpadding index, L2-normalize these auxiliary representations, concatenate them into z shaped [2B,D], and compute logits=z@z.T/0.2. Mask diagonal logits and use targets=(torch.arange(2*B, device=z.device)+B)%(2*B). Add 0.05*cross_entropy(logits, targets) to BPR. Mask other contrastive pairs sharing the same user or final training target to reduce false negatives, while retaining each designated positive pair. Do not normalize the recommendation scoring features unless separately evaluated. Start with existing dropout=0.2. Both views share one network and optimizer; inference uses one deterministic encoder pass with dropout disabled and one checkpoint per category. Do not copy DuoRec's count-1 readout, which assumes a different padding convention.
